A1.justification: Both PDFs describe AlignPose and retain the same central method. Text, equations, tables, figures, and appendices A-C in v1 and A-D in v2 could be inspected and matched reliably.

before.justification: v1 reports original multi-view pose-estimation results on four datasets, component and sensitivity ablations, qualitative examples, and runtime measurements.

after.justification: v2 retains original experiments and adds industrial-dataset evaluations, detector-quality experiments, and documented failure cases.

M1.justification: Section 3 retains the same NMS aggregation, frozen-feature representations, joint multi-view loss, Levenberg-Marquardt optimization, and scoring. FOSOD names the previously described detector pipeline. Revisions concern upstream experimental inputs and implementation documentation rather than a new AlignPose aggregation or refinement component.

E1.justification: Evaluation expands from four to six datasets by adding IPD and XYZ-IBD, substantially broadening industrial-object coverage. YCB-V, T-LESS, HouseCat6D, and ITODD-MV remain; their redistribution among tables does not represent removed coverage.

E2.justification: The pose-estimation comparator set is retained. New Appendix B.5/Table 14 introduces a detector comparison involving 3PT and CNOS (SAM) alongside the existing detector, now called FOSOD. These are detector alternatives, not new competing multi-view pose estimators; FreezeV2 is discussed through an approximation rather than directly evaluated.

E3.justification: ITODD-MV changes from the authors' GroundingDINO-based detector to 3PT detections with SAM2 segmentation. Industrial evaluation now reports AP without the previously reported ITODD AR metrics. New Table 14 systematically varies three detectors across industrial datasets and evaluates detection AP, AR10, and AR100 alongside pose AP, adding a substantial experimental protocol.

E4.justification: v2 adds detector-quality sensitivity experiments in B.5 and three failure case studies in Appendix D/Figures 9-11. Conversely, B.2 replaces v1's two-dataset NMS analysis of four representations and intra/inter-class suppression with a smaller T-LESS table comparing axis-aligned boxes and spheres. Cost-function and scoring analyses are retained.

E5.justification: Both versions report refinement runtime as mean plus standard deviation, with identical AlignPose timing values. Added CosyPose timings extend that reporting practice. Neither version reports pose-accuracy confidence intervals, significance tests, seeds, or repeated-run counts.

E6.justification: New industrial results include AlignPose AP of 79.8 on IPD and 66.5 on XYZ-IBD. HouseCat6D results change from 85.6 AR/85.8 AP to 88.9/89.6, and ITODD-MV AP changes from 73.2 to 76.8; changed or newly specified candidate-generation settings prevent treating these as established same-setting gains. Detector, failure-case, and baseline-timing results are added, while feature-ablation values also change. Main YCB-V, T-LESS, and seen-object T-LESS comparisons remain numerically unchanged.

T1.justification: The pose formulation and Equations 1-3 are mathematically unchanged. Neither version adds formal propositions, proofs, or substantive derivations. The new calibration discussion qualifies applicability rather than introducing a new mathematical assumption.

C1.justification: The abstract and contribution list expand the claimed evaluation scope from four to six datasets. The introduction replaces the 11% single-view and 5% multi-view advantage claims with a claim exceeding 14% on industrial datasets. The training-free, symmetry-agnostic, joint-refinement contributions remain unchanged.

C2.justification: New Appendix D explains failures from similar viewpoints with occlusion, large initial depth errors, and near-symmetric objects, and discusses calibration dependence. B.5 adds interpretation of detector dependence and partial compensation through multi-view aggregation. The unconditional memory-saving statement is qualified, and the previous numerical memory comparison is removed.

D1.justification: Appendix A newly specifies Co-Op inputs for all YCB-V/T-LESS ablations, an intermediate FoundPose feature-refinement step, directional lighting for textureless objects, and the industrial 3PT/SAM2 setup. Runtime scope and scaling are clarified, with CosyPose timing context added. Most existing hyperparameters, hardware details, and access information remain unchanged; newly documented steps alone do not establish when they were introduced.

R1.justification: v2 adds references for IPD, XYZ-IBD, 3PT, and FreezeV2. B.2 newly relates spherical NMS to FreezeV2's translation-distance suppression and acknowledges limits to direct comparison. The main related-work positioning remains stable; other bibliography updates largely concern formatting or publication metadata.

P1.justification: The overall narrative and section sequence remain intact. v2 revises dataset and implementation descriptions, condenses the NMS and cost-function discussions, introduces B.5 and Appendix D, names FOSOD, and makes local language, author-name, and bibliography edits. Most existing prose is retained.

P2.justification: The main and appendix benchmark tables are substantially reorganized into separate classic, HouseCat6D, and industrial comparisons. Two NMS heatmaps are replaced by a compact table; a detector table and three failure-case figures are added. Several existing qualitative montages are reproduced at higher resolution. The method diagrams and cost-function heatmaps are retained.

improvement.justification: The detector-quality study and concrete failure cases improve understanding of when AlignPose succeeds and fails, while IPD and XYZ-IBD strengthen industrial validation. Clearer implementation details and qualified memory claims also improve transparency. These are incremental gains over the already extensive validation in v1: the NMS evidence becomes narrower, and revised HouseCat6D/ITODD scores do not establish controlled performance improvements.
